utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we resume, I'd like to violate a custom, a custom which says that it's only in the month of January that you extend your best wishes for the next year. I violate this rule, it's the 1st of February, but I nevertheless on behalf of the Chamber wish everyone the best for 2016. Then I'd like to deal with a few matters on the court agenda before we start hearing further testimony. And I'd like to start with the Prosecution request for extensions to respond. On the 27th of January of this year, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting extensions of the deadlines for filing its responses to six of the nine bar table motions recently filed by the Defence. And the Chamber would like to inquire with the Defence if it has any position on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you for good wishes and same from the Defence for everybody here. We do not object to grant the Prosecution additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Considering the relatively large number of documents tendered in the Defence motions, the Chamber finds the Prosecution's request to be reasonable. It also notes that the Defence, as we now know, does not object. And the Chamber therefore grants the motion and sets the following deadlines: Responses to the third, sixth, and seventh motions shall be due on the 16 of February; and the responses to the fourth, the fifth, and the ninth motions shall be due on the 1st of March of 2016. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on this matter. Next item deals with the pending issue from the testimony of Dusan Pavlovic. It's about D1373. On the 14th of December of last year, during the testimony of Dusan Pavlovic, D1373, the witness's expert report was marked for identification pending the implementation of some corrections which can be found at transcript pages 42540 and 541. On the 5th of January, 2016, the Defence e-mailed the Prosecution and the Chamber advising that a revised version had been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 1D06200b. The Defence also stated that the revised report could be used in open session and that some of its content had been deleted. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace D1373 with the revised report uploaded under the number I just mentioned. Third and last matter I'd like to deal with at this moment deals with the withdrawal of a Prosecution. On the 30th of December of last year, the Prosecution sent a letter to the Victims and Witness Section requesting that witness Dusan Pavlovic identify and provide the Prosecution with specific material regarding his expert report and D1399 marked for identification. On 8th of January, 2016, the Prosecution informed the Chamber, the Defence, and the Victims and Witness Section via an e-mail that they wished to withdraw their request, and this withdrawal is hereby placed on the record. I leave it to that, although I have a few more items to be dealt with but at a later stage. Mr. MacDonald and Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. MacDonald, indeed, has a preliminary matter to raise, but before he did, I wanted to do two quick things. First, on behalf of the Prosecution to join the Bench and our colleagues in wishing all a Happy New Year. I'm actually not sure it's a violation of custom because maybe you get an extra day in a leap year, so we still may be within protocol. Secondly, I wanted to introduce to the Court a member of the Prosecution team who has not previously appeared in court and that is Ms. Sanhita Sen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in this courtroom, Ms. Sen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I thought everything would be later after the 28th of February and not before that, but this is a matter still to be discussed, Mr. Tieger. Perhaps we need expert evidence on that. Mr. MacDonald, there was a matter we were informed you would like to raise before we resume hearing the evidence of Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning. Your Honour, the Prosecution has provided a list of names to a court official. I think Your Honours have it. My colleague Mr. Lukic has a copy as well. We asked ICMP if we could refer to these names in public and open session just to double-check given that some confusion arose when we tried to refer to the list to certain -- a number of names down, for example, and there was some confusion from that. So if we can refer to these names in open session, Your Honours, I hope to lessen that confusion. The names contain all the ones that Mr. Lukic referred to in chief and the ones I intend to discuss with Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we were misinformed. We received indeed a list of 19 names with years of birth and we thought that was a list of names that should not be referred to in public session. But apparently it now turns that there's a green light for these names. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. These names can be referred to in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then clear that we know the names that are on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's also a copy for Mr. Pavlovic and I wondered if Your Honour wished to explain that to Mr. Pavlovic when he comes in, just to let the witness know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think can you do it yourself. There's no reason to -- to take over in this respect. Is Mr. Pavlovic on standby to enter the courtroom? Then he may be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to make sure where we stand, it's -- the Prosecution will start its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder, just to save time, Your Honour, if I could call up the first exhibit. It's D01399 MFI, the list provided by Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's D01399 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal, Mr. MacDonald. Good morning, Mr. Pavlovic. Before I remind that you're still bound by the solemn declaration, I'd like to extend our best wishes for 2016 to you as well, as we exchanged our best wishes with all in this courtroom. You're certainly not excluded. But now I then remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. MacDonald will now start his cross-examination. You'll find Mr. MacDonald to your right. Mr. MacDonald is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, I'd like to continue where you left off in direct examination and discuss the list that you brought with you when you came to The Hague to testify. Do you recall that list of individuals, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list of what specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's a list of individuals that you brought with you to the The Hague the first time you came to testify and that you provided to the Defence two days before that testimony, and it is entitled: "Overview of known individuals who died during breakthrough and other disputed cases." And I hope we can see it on the screen in front of us now.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, your theory, Mr. Pavlovic, is that the column that went from Srebrenica to Tuzla, various members of that column died in various ways and that the VRS went and picked up those bodies and bits of bodies and then buried them in mass graves. That's your theory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that can be called a theory. I did it on the basis of documents, eye-witness reports, intelligence reports of the BH army, your own experts, so I don't know if you can call it a theory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. That's what you're telling the Court happened. That's what you're advancing isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that there is a serious ground to believe that that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. And this list, it represents exhibits that you say support that theory, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of the examples that could lead one to the conclusion that that really happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now this list breaks down into various categories, and one of the categories is people you've identified because the DNA results show them as being labelled as being found in two different places; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of these persons were found - if those are the specific cases you mean - on the surface. Because many persons were found in two different places --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We're going to -- Mr. Pavlovic, just a moment. Yes, we're going to deal with specific examples now. I just wanted to identify the category for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 2 in the list in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, before I go any further, if I can just provide you with some information. Although this list is under seal so the public cannot see it, we checked with ICMP as to whether we could say some names in open session, and there is a list of names ICMP provided us with which the court official is giving you now. So I'd like to take you on the list to the name Mustafa Mehic. Do you see him on the list in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one I received now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, my apologies. I mean your list on the screen in front of you. Do you see the name Mustafa Mehic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, you discussed them in some length in your chief, and we can find that at transcript 42850 to 42854. And in your list you point that he is found partly -- or labelled as being found partly in Cancari Road 12 and partly at a place called Tisova Kosa. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can scroll down a little bit on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, those are the two sites he has been labelled, Cancari Road 12 and Tisova Kosa.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that what's I managed to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, are you aware that the evidence in this case shows that Cancari Road 12 is a secondary grave? Are you aware of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know off the cuff the list of secondary graves, but I'm not disputing that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And are you aware of evidence that shows that Cancari Road 12 is linked to a primary mass grave at Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't know by heart any of these connections, but I'm not disputing any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Are you aware of evidence that shows that a primary mass grave at Branjevo Military Farm was opened, filled with bodies, and shut by 17th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these details. I know the locality because I worked on the exhumation together with Mr. Jan Hensen in 2013, 2014, and we had certain doubts about this grave, but I don't know the operative details regarding the event itself for the example that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So you're not aware of evidence that shows that that primary mass grave was shut by July 17th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not work on that segment, but I'm not disputing what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So for your theory to be correct, someone would have to have picked up Mustafa Mehic, or most of him, carried it down to the road, and taken it to Branjevo Military Farm all before 17th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said before, I would not call it a theory. Furthermore, if we are talking about the reconstruction of all the events in Srebrenica in that period, there are witness reports that people were killed, the bodies were removed in sanitization, and that could include this person. So, yes, people died in combat, and one part of the mortal remains of this person was found there and the other part in Cancari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if you can just try on focus on what I'm asking you, Mr. Pavlovic, it is that for what you say to be correct, somebody would have had to picked up most of Mr. Mehic, carried it down to the road, and taken it to Branjevo Military Farm before 17th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would have to object at this moment. Because it's not what Mr. Pavlovic was claiming. It's what the Prosecution was actually claiming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That what's he is asking. Therefore whether he -- what his comment is on that claim --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in view of the fact that Mr. MacDonald put to the witness, the witness apparently unaware of it, that the Branjevo farm primary grave was shut on the 17th of July. So the witness is free to comment on that and that's what he is invited to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, apart from what may have happened in general for this specific case and irrespective of whether you are calling it a theory or whether you think it's the most reasonable explanation of what happened, which is often called by others a theory, but could you please respond directly in this specific case whether, in your view, that body then would have been sanitized, taken to the road, and brought to Branjevo farm before the 17th of -- or not later than the 17th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't have enough information about the creation of that grave and its progress to say whether it was brought from Branjevo or from Tisova Kosa to Cancari Road on the 12th. I don't know on what basis you are claiming that the grave was shut not later than the 17th July and whether some more bodies were added between the 17th and the date when it was opened again. Anything I would say would be speculation, and I don't know want to go into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do I then understand that you have no personal knowledge yourself about what happened to the Branjevo farm primary grave-site when it was shut, whether any bodies -- you have no knowledge about that? Because you are asking Mr. MacDonald where his knowledge comes from. Well, of course, most important is what the Chamber hears about it, and therefore you're invited to tell us whatever you would know about the date of shutting this primary grave and what may have happened after that. Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. No. [Interpretation] I don't have such knowledge. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Let's have a quick look at a map Mr. Pavlovic just to orient ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have P01087 on the screen, please. I'm looking for page 19. I wonder if the Court Officer could zoom in on the left-most blue arrow. It's about centre left of the screen, so -- just up slightly from that box. If we could just scroll up slightly that would be great. Yes, if we can stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, looking at the left blue arrow here, do you see the word "Baljkovica" that it goes through?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And just below it, not the first dotted red line but the second one, do you see the words "Tisova Kosa" written almost vertically?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 11 on this map, please -- in this map book, rather. And if we can rotate that -- yes, thank you. And perhaps scroll down. And that's fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, do you see about centre-left on this screen a word written in red, "Baljkovica"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And we know that just below that is Tisova Kosa. So again, for what you are telling the Court, Mr. Pavlovic, the VRS would have had to have come back down to the road, that's the black line on the map, and driven south, down past Orahovac where there was a mass execution and a mass grave, to Karakaj, and then all the way north, up past Kozluk, past another mass execution and mass grave-site, all the way up to Branjevo Military Farm in order to put the parts of Mustafa Mehic they'd found in the ground. For what you are telling the Court, that's what they would have had to have done; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, I never said that or claimed that. I said that the person was partly found in Tisova Kosa and partly at Cancari 12 grave-site so that -- that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Even if it were Cancari Road 12 for Mustafa Mehic, they would still have to have driven down past Orahovac, down past Zvornik, all the way down to the road where we see Cancari marked. So still passing a mass grave and a mass execution site, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As I've said, I did not seriously study these elements of circumstances in and around Srebrenica, whether they passed along one or another road or maybe took some local roads that we're not even aware that but that the locals are aware of, it's something I couldn't comment on. We just have the facts that are at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to another question about Mustafa Mehic. Are you aware what parts of Mustafa Mehic are labelled as being found in Tisova Kosa and what parts are labelled as being found in Cancari Road 12?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something that I could only ask you, because I had no access to the forensic findings and I think that you do have them. So how -- how could I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, we do have them, Mr. Pavlovic, but we disclosed them to the Defence, and I understood them to be amongst the things that you would have reviewed for your report. Did you not review the forensic findings?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Look, I reviewed some of it. I couldn't review everything because it's a massive material, too great for one man to review everything in a short time. What I needed was tracing the bodies. I tried to reconstruct some situations and I tried to get the facts that I needed. But what parts of a body were found in one or another location, I don't see what that would change substantially. Whether it was where there was combat, where people lost their lives, and which parts were found in a secondary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, you prepared a list of disputed cases, cases where not just facts are presented but where you say that there's dispute about this. Did you at least for the limited number of those appearing on your list, did you review the forensic information which was available? I'm not talking about the whole of the large numbers, but just those that you qualified as disputed. Did you review the forensics for those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you talk about forensic data, I did not have access to forensic findings such as photographs and from what body parts the samples of bones were taken and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you don't have to explain for me whether there were good reasons not do or to review the forensics. I just wanted to know whether did you or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have tried to clarify it. When you say "forensic findings," do you mean the forensic reports, the analysis of skeletons, or the types of wounds? It's something that did I not find. I'm not sure if it exists within the materials or not, but I did not find that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were not provided with it. You didn't ask for it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not even know that I could get it. I worked on the basis of what I did receive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And -- okay, I leave it to that. You say you had no access to those forensic results. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do. Mr. Pavlovic, Mr. MacDonald put it to that you this forensic material was handed over to the Defence who would have given it to you to review to prepare your report. Did the Defence not give you the material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received a database with, I suppose, half a million documents, and then I searched the database, looking for what I believed to be important. Now whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you what you did with it. I'm asking you did you receive any forensic material from the Defence for purposes of your report, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Directly receiving any autopsy reports from them, autopsy reports as such, then the answer would be no. If that is what you have in mind and if we have understood each other well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I have in mind is forensic material. So you didn't receive any forensic material from the Defence. That's your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not receive autopsy reports directly from them. I came across some forensic reports in the form of facts relating to certain exhumations. But autopsy reports as such, including photographs and everything else, is something that I never received and I did not find. I hope you understand me. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do not, but I'll leave it to Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, just one more questions on this point. You've worked for some years for missing persons institutes in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you worked closely with ICMP, and for Mustafa Mehic on your list, you're relying on ICMP data only. That's all correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not correct. I have used all materials that were at my disposal and that I received from the Defence. These were not only ICMP materials. In the republican centre --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just for Mustafa Mehic. If we can go back to your list, it's page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, the list is MFI D01399.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the English version be -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And for Mustafa Mehic, in your description, the only information you're quoting is -- it's DNA information. That's what you're relying on.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Pavlovic, given how far the VRS would have had to have driven if what you say to the Court is correct, we investigated this victim, we found the reassociation report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 33612. I'm looking for page 2 in the English and page 1 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, did you ask anybody for this reassociation report? ICMP, the Missing Persons Institute, the ICTY? Did you ask anybody for this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask anyone for this specific document because I did not consider it significantly important, which does not mean that it is unimportant, because I had information that the person was found in these two localities and that was sufficient for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Well, perhaps we can discuss why this might be important. Now you see it's talking about Mustafa Mehic, and you see where it says "measures taken." It's towards the bottom in B/C/S. I'm just going to read out what it says underneath that: "Association of missing main part of the lower jaw (two-thirds of the skeleton) marked as TS1-1-MNT1-M to the mortal remains previously buried and marked as CR-12B-161. "Fracture lines of bones correspond fully." So, Mr. Pavlovic, what's been found in Tisova Kosa, it's two-thirds of a jaw bone. You see that there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we turn over the page just in the B/C/S, and if we can just have the B/C/S on the screen, and I wonder if the Court Officer could zoom in on the left-hand side of that photograph, the extreme left where the label TS1 is. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And, Mr. Pavlovic, I'm not a forensic pathologist but that -- the bone in the -- with the label appears to be about two-thirds of a jaw bone. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For my guidance, Mr. MacDonald, which one are you looking at? I see the marking TS1 but I don't see which bone you are referring to as the left jaw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think underneath the marking there is a bone, I think it's actually in a bag which is outlined by the green, and it's the bone underneath the marking that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, we wrote to ICMP to ask them to check their findings and they replied to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 33625 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is a letter from ICMP to us here at the ICTY. Now, it's relatively long, but it deals with the reassociation of Mustafa Mehic based on DNA matches. I would like to take you to the second paragraph. I'm just going to read the third line, sentence beginning "In situ," and that line reads: "In situ photographs at the grave-site show an intact head associated with this body including a complete mandible and later autopsy photographs also show a mandible present." And if we can go to the last paragraph, and I'm going to read the first sentence: "The documented presence of a fully articulated mandible associated with the remains of Mustafa Mehic at the time of recovery from the CR 12 grave indicates that this mandible was inadvertently separated from its original case at some later point in time and came to be mistakenly put in with remains considered to be from Tisova and submitted for DNA testing." Mr. Pavlovic, "mandible" is just another word for "jaw bone," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are expert terms used by anthropologists and pathologists, I don't know if that's exactly what it means, but I don't dispute that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Two questions, then, Mr. Pavlovic. Seeing as ICMP has confirmed that all the remains we have for Mustafa Mehic, in fact, were exhumed from Cancari Road 12 and that this is just a simple case of mislabelling now corrected, this example doesn't support your theory or what you're telling this Court that there was any asanacija after combat, does it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see -- may I answer? Yes? All right. Thank you. This tells me that the ICMP is making errors and this raises the issue how many errors like this there could be. What does it mean that they have mixed up the bones? Because bone samples are labelled in situ where exhumation is carried out, and a bone sample from Tisova Kosa was labelled during asanacija rather than for ICMP giving it a label or a name later on. Also when a forensic expert takes a bone sample for the DNA, he is the one who gives a label to the bone sample. He is the person who is authorised by the Prosecutor to do so and not by the ICMP. So I find this astonishing what you have read now, that they've mixed up the bone and then returned the bone. We are serious people. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, if you just answer my question. Given that all of Mustafa Mehic came from Cancari Road 12, he does not support what you're telling this Court about asanacija at all, does he?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously Mr. Pavlovic doubts this report and we really need then the report from ICMP, how many mistakes were made like this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that's a different question. A very interesting question, by the way, but a different question. And that Mr. Pavlovic does not rely on this report is not true because a second ago he told us how shocking it is. And would it be shocking if you wouldn't believe it? No, I think he calls it shocking because he believes it. So, therefore, I tend to disagree with you on whether Mr. Pavlovic relies on it or not. Mr. Pavlovic, there are two clearly distinct questions. The one was the one that was put to you by Mr. MacDonald and the other one was the question you would like to draw our attention to. Now you have done the second, that you are amazed by these kind of mistakes to be made. Could you now please answer the first question whether this report supports or does not support - rather, the contrary - to what you have pointed at, that is, that the body parts were found in a place different from what this letter now tell us they came from, that is, Cancari Road 12. Could you please answer that question now first. You've answered the second question you posed yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hm. In order to answer this question, we have to see when the sanitation at Tisova Kosa was carried out. I think it was at some point before the exhumation at another location - that's Cancari Road 12 - and then when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were not invited to further elaborate on possible other problems that may exist in this context. You were invited to tell us whether this report does support your theory or what you want to draw our attention to in your list of disputed matters or whether it does, rather, not. Could you please tell us, apart from what further had to be perhaps researched, whether this report supports your views or whether this report does not support your views.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I could see from this document, it does not support my views. It, rather, refutes them. For me it raises a number of other issues about what is illogical with regard to this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've drawn our attention to that already before, and you've now answered the question that was put to you as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, I'm looking at the clock. I don't know whether you are inclined to finish within one or two minutes. If not, we'd rather take the break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's certainly within three or four minutes, Your Honour. I just have to show Mr. Pavlovic one more thing and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And if that concludes this -- this specific portion --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And then ask one question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, then, and finish within the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I appreciate it's the first time that you will have seen this letter and you told the Court, amongst other things, that sometimes bones are labelled in situ at the exhumation. So I thought we could look at the photographs of Mustafa Mehic when he is exhumed. So just before we leave this document, if I can draw your attention or I'll simply say Mustafa Mehic is labelled as CR-12B-161.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we can have on the screen 65 ter number 33613. Now this is the typed autopsy report for CR-12B-161. If we can move to the second page, please, in both languages. And if we can just have the English here, that's where the photographs are. Can we rotate that, please, by 180 degrees. Thank you. And if we can zoom in perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is Mustafa Mehic in the grave, Mr. Pavlovic. There we see his arm and his head, the head facing left. And from what we can see there, the jaw bone, or mandible, seems intact. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It takes really an anthropologist and a pathologist to say something like that. I cannot say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we turn to the final page in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, this is a -- Mustafa Mehic on the autopsy table. And just underneath the skull, would you agree with me that we see a full jaw bone, or mandible, there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in on the upper part of the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I don't know when this photograph was made, whether it was after the association -- or, rather, would you repeat the question? I want to make sure I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you, Mr. Pavlovic, this is a photograph taken at the time he was exhumed. And the question is: Underneath the skull we see a complete jaw bone, don't we?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I'm not an expert in the field, I can only say that an expert has to establish that, and then I will agree. That's one. And, two, how is it possible that if the body was exhumed whole like that, a part of it ended up in different bags?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Pavlovic, the Court isn't here to answer your questions. I just have one more for you before we take the break.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Given that Mustafa Mehic was the only one in this category that you spoke about, you mentioned a couple of other names, but Mustafa Mehic was the only one from this DNA category of your list that you discussed, why did you think it was sufficient simply to look at the ICMP data and do no further investigation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this is not the only such case in my report. There are more. Certain names coincide with the names of persons who are included in the reports of your experts as found both on the surface and in mass graves. That's why I was surprised when Mr. McCloskey [sic] got on his feet right now saying that they had never had such evidence. So basically this is not the only example of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I know it's not the only example. We will be dealing with other examples. He was -- Mustafa Mehic was the only one that you discussed at length. Why did you think it was sufficient simply to look at the ICMP data and not investigate further?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, it's not the only one. I listed more and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness, there's no need to repeat an answer which was not an answer to the question. Would you please focus on the question. Why was there no need to further investigate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I understood the first part of the question to claim that it's the only example of this kind. And that's the first part only. Now I'm trying to answer the second part of the question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I agree with you completely that this kind of analysis is necessary in each and every case. Unfortunately, at that moment, it was not objectively possible for me to go into deeper analysis. And I agree with you completely that in each and every case this kind of thorough analysis is necessary, especially when bodies that are found could be symptomatic for different reasons. If I had the same possibilities and capacities as you did, I would have done a much more thorough analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm happy to take the break now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break. Witness, perhaps during the break you would think about directly answering questions rather than to first answer questions you have on your mind. If they are relevant, the Defence will certainly put them to you at any later stage. We'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, so that is at 11.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I neglected to tender the documents that we discussed about Mustafa Mehic. I have spoken briefly with Mr. Lukic. I understand there's no objection. So I would tender 65 ter 33612, that's the reassociation report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 33612 receives number P7789.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: 33613, that's the autopsy with the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 33613 receives number P7790.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And finally, 65 ter 33625, the letter from ICMP addressed to Peter McCloskey dated 27 January 2016.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 33625 receives number P7791.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder if, again to save time Your Honours, we could call up the first exhibit I plan to use. That's D01399, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 6 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And it's under seal? And it must not be published.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'd like to discuss one more example with you from the category of people labelled as being in two different places. The list that you brought is going to appear on the screen in front of you in a moment. Do you see the heading in B/C/S "asanacija," in English "sanitization"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The third name down, Mr. Pavlovic, again it's been cleared by ICMP as Salkic, Nizam. And in the description part of your lists, you write: "Found in mass grave Zeleni Jadar 5 and 6." Are you aware that the evidence in this case shows both of those graves are secondary mass graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that. However, these persons, apart from the first two, should not be here at all. This is part of my work analysis. There's obviously a confusion if the Defence provided it to you. What I submitted is a table at a later stage more finalized. This is just part of my preliminary work where I only listed cases that could potentially be interesting. So that numbers 3, 4, and 5 and 6, do not fall into the category of bodies that were partly sanitized and partly found in mass graves. This is a list of bodies that could potentially be interesting and deserve further investigation. It's by mistake they remained in this table. I'm not disputing, however, that these graves are secondary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So is this not the table that you submitted to the Defence and that you're advancing before the Court?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just explained. I had a working table, a table with names that I could work on later. I had given it to the Defence, yes, but I also gave them a more finalized table. I believe that these names remained here by mistake because there was some confusion just before my coming to testify. I don't know exactly why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I'm also addressing Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, this list was presented as -- as I understood it, as the latest list provided to you by Mr. Pavlovic, but now Mr. Pavlovic claims that there must be a more updated list. Do you have any knowledge about that? And, Mr. Pavlovic, I think that - I'm just talking from my recollection - that you provided this list just a couple of days before you testified in this court in December. When did you give the newest list? Or did you provide that updated list after your testimony or still before your testimony? Or did you only provide one list and did you never give an updated list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I explained the last time I was here, I brought this with me and I showed to the Defence what I had, and it was a working document, a working table. After that, I made a short list that I also gave to the Defence. I suppose it's by mistake that this one remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you give the short list, prior to your testimony in December or after you testified in December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I started testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are you aware of any shorter list the witness would have provided you with?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This the first time I heard so I'm trying to check in my computer if I have anything shorter. I cannot locate it but I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps meanwhile we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- to check with my case manager as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps meanwhile we'll continue and -- because this comes really a bit as a surprise, especially since the witness emphasised that, as he said on page 19, "we are serious people," so we are serious enough to only look at final lists. By the way, you list you presented, Mr. Pavlovic, does not -- where do -- could we see that it is not -- it's just a list of matters that needed to be further researched. It says that it's -- that the title suggests otherwise. But if it's a preliminary working document, of course, that should not be final but ... how could we have known, also in view of your evidence given in December, that this was not what it claims to be? That's an: "Overview of known individual who died during breakthrough and other disputed cases." That's how it's titled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, there are several questions in this one. The way in which you could know -- in fact, it wasn't planned to present this. I just put them in as something that could be interesting. For instance, the last three persons, as we see, were found in two primary graves. That opens up the possibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that there had been sanitization if they were in primary graves, but that's an operative piece of data. I did not later exclude them. Errors are possible. This is a technical matter purely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although it's not an answer to my question, I do understand what you want to tell us. Mr. Lukic, any response yet? If not, I'll invite Mr. MacDonald to proceed. But it is a bit on a shaky basis that we're proceeding if we don't know whether there's any shorter list in which perhaps some of the items Mr. MacDonald would like to deal with are not appearing anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we should ask Mr. Pavlovic to check the whole document and see what should be excluded from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- but apparently he has done that already, as he said. Do you have a copy of the most -- the most recent version of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I have it, but I could look for it today when I go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you mean you have it somewhere with you in The Hague, I take it? You're not telling us --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether I have it with me. I would have to check. Last time I brought it and handed it over. Later today, I could look at this and -- these things are obviously from a different preparatory preliminary level. This is a technical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we're dealing with a technical error for weeks and weeks in preparing for today's hearing. Would you -- if Mr. MacDonald draws your attention to any item on this list which you say shouldn't be there any further, would you immediately tell us at the very beginning. And then, Mr. MacDonald, I leave it in your hands whether -- if the item you addressed is not on the list anymore, then it shouldn't be there, then I wonder whether it's worth any further attention. But perhaps you have a few more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'm not going to deal with any more of the DNA category, but I do want to ask you one question in general about it. You just stated to the Court that some of these people are pulled out of primary mass graves, and I note that the fourth and the sixth one were pulled from -- or exhumed, rather, from Glogova 5 and 7, and Ravnice 1 and 2. Are you aware that those graves are linked to the execution at Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing these facts if you have them. I just included these in order to investigate further and see what it could be about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pavlovic, if you just --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- why one person was found in two primary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If you'll bear with me now. Well, in Kravica warehouse, the evidence shows the execution was carried out with guns and with numerous hand-grenades. So if amongst the packed bodies in Kravica warehouse a hand-grenade rips a person in two, that would explain - or could explain - why one person ends up in two primary mass graves; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just suggest a way of efficiency, Mr. Pavlovic. When the question is are you aware of it, it's not necessary for you say "I don't dispute." Just say whether you are aware or not aware, and your answers will be much shorter and we can make better progress. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then perhaps your response to the suggestion put to you by Mr. MacDonald that if people are killed through a hand-grenade, whether you would agree - at least that's how I understand the question - that if a body is torn apart in several pieces as a result of this type of killing, whether that could reasonably explain various body parts to have been found in more than one primary grave, primary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is a possibility for a hand-grenade to tear a body apart into several pieces, then, yes; but I don't know whether a hand-grenade can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Let's move to another part of the list, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can go to page 8 in the English and I would suggest we just have the English at this point. And that should not be broadcast, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now this is the second half of your report, and I understand you testified in chief that this was a separate list at the beginning but the Defence have -- have presented it all as one. But you recall this part of your list, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my analysis on the same subject but in a different form.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my first question, I suppose, should be: Do you recognise if this is just a working copy or is this a final -- finalized copy that you wish to present to the Court?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the final version. It could be improved on, but this is how far I got.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Well, as I understand this part of your report, you list a number of names out to the right-hand side there, and you list them there because the word "eksploziva" appears under cause of death in the death certificate. That's why they're on this list, yes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that the injuries were sustained by explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Just to go over what you said about these people and I just want you to confirm for me that it's correct. At transcript page 42868, line 11, in your examination-in-chief, you said the following: "The next group of examples refers to persons who appear in death certificates that are issued after the final identification has been done and are issued by the court. So next to the report of final identification a death certificate is issued. On the other side of the document towards the bottom, cause of death is mentioned. And while examining certificates of death, in some examples I observed that some persons had a sustained injuries from explosive devices and those persons were exhumed from graves." I'm right in saying you put this forward as support of what you say because you're aware that members of the column were exposed to shelling, minefields, as you say, the occasional suicide by hand-grenade, and because these death certificates have the word "eksploziva," you cite them in support of what you are saying. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about death certificates issued upon final identification by the acting pathologist who was authorised to perform this work by the prosecutor's office, not issued by the court. And in these death certificates, on the other side, on the flip side, cause of death is indicated. And I did find certain cases where persons were killed by blast wounds and were found in graves, and knowing the circumstances of the movement of the column and the attacks they were under, one can conclude that some of these people who -- killed trying the breakout ended up after sanitization in these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, Mr. Lukic only discussed one example with you and that was Alic Husein, and on the list in front of us, we see him in the third row off to the right in the second column. Now, what you said about Alic Husein, and this is at transcript page 42870, line 15, is: "While reviewing the certificate of death that is signed by the pathologist in the investigation, I saw that the injuries the person sustained were of -- were caused by explosives." Do you recall saying that about this death certificate?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably said that. Because it says here that the injuries were caused by mines and explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Did you review that death certificate personally, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 33617 on the screen, please. I think we can just do this with the B/C/S, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, we see the name Alic Husein there; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now box 21 is cause of death. Can you just read out for us the B/C/S statement of the cause of death, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Gun-shot or explosion, destruction of the head."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, you've written the word -- or you've testified the word "eksploziva" appeared in the cause of death, but you didn't mention that the word "gun-shot" also appeared there, did you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned examples where explosion is mentioned. I see that there's gun-shot as well mentioned here, but I don't see what that really changes. I can explain further if you'd like me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I understood you to be telling the Court that you had determined these people died by explosive devices on the basis of what's said in the death certificate. Now, the death certificate says gun-shot/explosive. I understood it to be supporting your theory because you talked about how the people in the column were subject to shelling or maybe stepped on minefields. But if this cause of death could be gun-shot or explosive, then it doesn't support your -- well, what you're telling the Court at all, does it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood that destruction was caused both by gun-shot and explosion. The fact that it's gun-shot too doesn't have to mean anything in itself because there were persons who were exhumed from mass graves who had only gun-shot wounds, because we know that some people lost their lives because of injuries inflicted with infantry weapons during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I just ask you now, you say it could be that that person died through a gun-shot and an explosion. Just for me to understand what you mean. Do you mean to say that simultaneously with a shot fired at that person hitting, for example, his head, which is the example here, that at the same time, simultaneously, there was an explosion which then also destroyed his head? So a blast and a gun-shot hitting the head exactly at the same time? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we talk about reconstruction, I don't see a need to draw such a conclusion because it does not necessarily mean that it happened simultaneously. The person may have been injured after falling to the ground, for example, if a shell landed there, then it could be shrapnel. So there's no need to assert that it happened simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But have you considered that it's possible that the head was destroyed in such a way that it is very difficult to say whether it was the result of a gun-shot or an explosion so that it's either of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's a question for experts who are of this particular profession. One or two of them should provide their opinions. I just mention what the pathologist stated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and you draw all kind of conclusions on the basis of that and those conclusions are based on a certain interpretation of what this expert said. That is, that it was through an explosive that he died, and that's why you think he must have been in the column because that's where you would find these kind of blasts, isn't it? That's your reasoning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just one of many examples where there are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness -- Witness, I'm not talking about other examples. I'm focussing on this one. Did I present your reasoning well? Or did I make any mistake in that respect? In this particular case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said it could be, or may be. There is this possibility that this could have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you leave it open that it may have been by a gun-shot wound as well, instead of an explosive wound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would undermine any type of conclusion as you've drawn from this -- from this cause of death report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The destruction of the head by explosion is not excluded here as a possibility. It's included, rather, as one of the possibilities. So that is why I took it into consideration and included in my report as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you're telling us is that you cannot exclude that they had -- on the basis of your material, you cannot exclude that they were killed when being in a column on the basis of a few assumptions, that that's where blast wounds were taking place and that's where people were killed by gun-shots. It's all open.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only raised certain issues because I cannot make the reconstruction, the forensic reconstruction. I just raised certain issues by specific evidence on the basis of the information that we have about the movement of the column and also the incidents that happened. That would include the events that took place on the ground and also the source of injuries that people sustained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, do you know how many names and how many grave-sites you cite in this part of your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That wasn't so important for me at all. I think that there was a sufficient number of cases that one could think along certain lines. I know that there are many other such cases and I think it's not disputed at all. I suppose that you've analysed who died because of blast wounds in terms of specific graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, we looked at the entire list, if that's what you mean, Mr. Pavlovic, and there are 83 persons you cite from 12 different graves. Now, six of the graves are linked to Kravica warehouse and six are not, and 42 of these death certificates come from victims found in graves not linked to Kravica warehouse. Mr. Pavlovic, are you aware, every single one of those 42 death certificates, every single one says gun-shot/explosive on it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I do not dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So His Honour Judge Orie's reasoning when he says that, in essence, it's all open, you can't conclude on the basis of these death certificates, that applies to all 42 of those death certificates. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never asserted that I drew the conclusion that it was so. I just said that I opened up certain possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to deal with another category in your list, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can turn to Mr. Pavlovic's list that he brought with him, D01399 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And perhaps we can go into page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, the last category I want to deal with is a category where you found a statement of a person walking in the column who said that he saw another person die, and that's the majority of the people in this first half of the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. MacDonald, but I would like to ask one additional question in relation to what we dealt with earlier. I read from your transcript of today when you were talking about death certificate issued upon final identification, et cetera. You said: "And I did find certain cases where persons were killed by blast wounds and were found in graves. And knowing the circumstances of the movement of the column and the attacks they were under, one can conclude that some of these people who killed," and then there's a small portion illegible, "trying the breakout ended up after sanitization in these graves." You said: "I did find certain cases where persons were killed by blast wounds." From the 42 autopsy reports, it does not establish that they were killed by blast wounds. I think that's what you testified later this morning. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I didn't understand you quite well. Do I agree with what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That you later this morning testified that the cases you were referring to did not indicate that they were killed by blast wounds but that they indicate that they possibly were killed by blast wounds, possibly by gun-shots.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just look at the question, please. I am not certain that I understand this quite clearly. Let me try to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'd rather you to answer my questions. I did read to you a portion of your -- of the transcript of today of your testimony in which you said you did find certain cases where persons were killed by blast wounds and were found in graves. From what I understood in your testimony later is that you did not find indicated that people were killed by blast wounds but that people could have been killed either by blast wounds or by gun-shots. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the first part I already said that I agree with that. The second part, I have said that I understood what I read, that they died by both gun-shot and blast wounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's what -- that was your initial explanation. I think later on you even withdrew that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not withdraw it. I only said that on the basis of examples which I list, I left the possibility that some of them may have been killed by blast wounds and that it may have happened during their breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you were more pertinent earlier in your testimony. You said you found cases where persons were killed by blast wounds, whereas you now say possibly they may have been killed by blast wounds. And then you drew conclusions, "one can conclude that some of these people," and then you said it was during the breakthrough. That's all shaky conclusions on a shaky factual basis, isn't it? Because you could also conclude otherwise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a typical reconstruction. If you have information that thousands of people died during the breakthrough in the way that they died, and when you're looking for the bodies there's nowhere else for them to be, there's a possibility that they're in graves, so then you look for certain evidence that could support conclusions that are directed that way. You have the number of missing persons in connection with Srebrenica. They are all in the list, both those who died during the breakthrough and those who were taken prisoner, those who perished there. Just one list of missing persons. So it's logical that you try to determine where the thousands of people who died during the breakthrough in the way that they did are buried. Where could they be? So it's something that's basic in my trade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are explaining a long search for persons to be found. You are not responding to my question. I leave it to that. Mr. MacDonald. But one thing: If you say you only raise issues, whereas you say you can conclude, that's more than raising an issue. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To conclude that there is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And, Mr. Pavlovic, I'm going to back to deal with the last category in your list that you want to deal with. That is, persons where you find a statement, persons -- of persons walking in the column who say that they saw someone die and name that person. Now, I'm right in saying that the person identifying the victim is also part of the column. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's a case in which a person from a column saw somebody die, then it's logical that that person was also a member of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. And as these people are dying when they're under attack, it means that the person identifying them is also under attack at that time, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be so but not necessarily. He could have seen him later on as he walked by. There are such statements where they saw a group of people who had been killed by a shell, and the person stating that walked along perhaps half an hour later. So everything that you are saying is an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We'll come back to that. For those people who do identify when they see the person die, they're being attacked by heavy artillery, anti-aircraft munitions, potentially there are minefields. These are all ways that people in the column died; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's noted in the statements the various ways in which people died, and I quoted that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, the vast -- well, of the approximately 20 victims here that were exhumed from mass graves, only one of them is identified by a family member. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the final identification on the basis of DNA or were they recognised when they died? What specifically do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm talking about the category where you find somebody who has given a statement that they see somebody die. In that category, from the people exhumed later from mass graves, only one of them is identified by a family member. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look into the number of such persons. If I say "identified," that is to say, saw him being killed during breakthrough, if that's what you mean by being identified. Simply as a category. Because identification that I had in mind is final identification based on DNA analysis, if you talk about that. If you talk about one person seeing another being killed during breakthrough and identifying him in that sense, there is just one case where a family member saw another person being killed during the breakthrough, it's possible. Have I understood your question well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you have. Just for the avoidance of confusion, I know that you say witness X saw victim Y die in such and such a place, and then you also tend to say where this person was exhumed from, the part I'm focussing on is just where witness X saw victim Y die, not where they were exhumed from. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now the column, the terrain that it's moving through is mainly mountainous and heavily forested; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, did it ever occur to you that a person who is under attack from heavy artillery or anti-aircraft munitions who is seeing people die around them, when those people are not family members, who is presumably terrified that they might die at any point in heavily forested mountainous terrain, maybe they get their identifications wrong of the person who died?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's theoretical, and theoretically it is certainly possible. But if we deal with these matters seriously, then we try to reconstruct what happened. And then we know that the column moved in such a way that people from the same formations from the same places, people who knew one another, I'm talking about something from the statements, went together. Family members, neighbours from the same places, people who knew one another tended to stick together and move together. These were also people who had four years of war experience and combat experience behind them, so these were not people who didn't know what to do in such a situation. Of course, their lives were in danger but they were used to such circumstances and that has to be taken into account. But theoretically, of course, anything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I think you answered my question with your first line there, and I would like to move to a concrete example to look at this. Now, if I can draw your attention to the name Amir Zukanovic, third down in the B/C/S, fifth down in the English. And the witness statement you cite says that he died in the beginning of the breakthrough towards Buljim and you then go on to point out he was exhumed from Cerska. Are you aware of the evidence regarding the Cerska grave-site, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not a subject of my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Let me just give you a brief resume of it. The evidence shows that three buses full of arrested people were seen turning down that road, followed by other vehicles with Bosnian Serb soldiers in them, and thereafter gun-fire was heard. And in terms of forensic evidence, 150 bodies were taken from the primary mass grave at Cerska. 149 of them were determined to have been killed by gun-shot wounds, the last one as an undetermined cause of death, and 48 of the bodies exhumed from that grave had ligatures. Now, bearing that in mind, Mr. Pavlovic, let's look at the witness statement that you cite here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 33589 on the screen, please, and it's page 1 of both languages. Now, in the B/C/S, it's about ten lines down and it's underlined. In the English we see the second name about six lines up from the bottom which is in capitals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, I just want to read that line to you, Mr. Pavlovic. In this statement, it says: "Immediately after we took off from Buljim, I saw Amir Zukanovic, from Brakovci, Srebrenica municipality, died from the shrapnel of the shell." You see those words, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, mm-hm. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at the forensic evidence dealing with this victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we please turn to P01982, and this is not to be broadcast. And if we turn to page 7 and I'm looking for line 85.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, you see the name Amir Zukanovic. And a few columns along, you see the grave-site code CSK-37. Do you see that, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So let's look at his autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number 04550a. Is there a B/C/S version of this as well, I think? Yes. We see in the top left case number CSK-37 and towards the bottom of the page, under the heading "External examination" we see: "Condition: Complete." And if we can turn the page in both documents. If we look down at the bottom the heading "Evidence of trauma," we see two entries that are not post-mortem. The first, a high-velocity gun-shot wound, 9 millimetres, which is going from the back of the skull out through the front, from left to right; and a gun-shot wound on left shoulder-blade. And if we can turn to the last page here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps for those are not familiar with the sirens it's the -- every month the system is tested at Monday, the first day of the month -- first Monday of the month at 12.00 sharp. That's what you hear at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My apologies. It's actually page 3 I'm looking for in both documents. Now just under the heading "Other evidence," we see: "Wire cuff and assorted wire found loose in body bag." And the Prosecution's position is that that is a ligature found on Mr. Zukanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, when the evidence in the autopsy report conflicts so strongly with that in the witness statement, wouldn't you agree with me that in this case the witness you cite simply got his identification wrong?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several possibilities, including that one. What is interesting is that the bullet is of a larger calibre than average, and pathologists can concentrate on that type of wound instead of ligatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt but I'm not asking you to expand upon the autopsy report. I think you answered my question, when you --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: -- in the first line there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I have one last question and then I think it may be time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Did you do any further investigation, any follow-up, anything, for this victim, Amir Zukanovic, apart from find this statement that you cite here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything further would be forensic expert work, and that's done by the official of the prosecutor, not me.
