I suppose that all persons who are on the list were subjected to this type of analysis, whether they got killed or they're executed, what type of wound, et cetera. The question is whether pathologists and anthropologists had information about the movement of the column and different ways of death --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, that was not my question. My question was: Did you do any further investigation on the victim Amir Zukanovic apart from looking at and citing to the statement that you cite in the list? Did you do any further investigation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not. But should we understand your answer to be that you did not go beyond the statement you quoted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this specific case, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we were talking about this specific case. Thank you for that, clarifying your answer. Time for a break. Witness, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, I think you scheduled for three hours of cross. Are you on track?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I hope so, Your Honour. I'm not 100 per cent sure because I'm not sure how much time has been used by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you could ask Madam Registrar and she'll tell you. We'll hear that after we resume. We take a break and we'll resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to come into the courtroom, having looked at the time and I am afraid that the Judges took some time as well ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that I take it you've quite some time left. Any chance that we could conclude the cross-examination today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Certainly today, Your Honour, and I would hope next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try to aim at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'd like to continue looking at some examples from the category that we were dealing with; that is, people who testified they saw someone die in the column. Now, at transcript page 42866, line 3, you said you took examples "where the eye-witness said they saw an individual die or get killed, not that they heard but that they actually saw the person dying or being killed." And a little further on, after the Presiding Judge asks you a question to clarify, you say, and this is transcript page 42866, lines 14 to 18: "All right. Very well. I'm not sure if we can mention names. Here the way it is phrased in the comment, perhaps it's not precise enough, but I was taking examples that I mentioned; i.e., exclusively examples where a witness said that they actually were an eye-witness and saw the person get killed or die." Do you remember saying that, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that then; but after seeing this list, including cases that shouldn't be there, I cannot rule out the possibility that a working version of the list did not exclude the cases where there are witness reports saying that they had seen somebody die. Such cases should be excluded, and I see that the list is not the one I was thinking I was commenting upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the right time to interrupt briefly. Mr. Lukic, any results from the updated new list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot locate anything apart that we uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pavlovic, the Defence is not aware of any better or newer or updated list you are talking about. Have you -- you have had no opportunity yet to look at it. Perhaps you do that this afternoon to see whether there's any better one. And we're still puzzled by what happened. Let's leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Pavlovic, I'd like to take you to one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can have the list on the screen, please, MFI D01399. It's page 5 in the English, page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And again, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I can say at this point we are going to be moving between the lists and witness statements for the next few examples, so perhaps to spare my blushes, I can say whenever it's MFI D01399 it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm looking for the name here Azem Pasalic. He is the second name down in the English and about the 12th name down in the B/C/S, four from the bottom. Do see him there, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is the witness -- the victim, sorry, you were discussing when His Honour Judge Orie asked you the question about how you selected examples. And that can be found at transcript page 42864 to 42866. So let's look at the witness statement you cite here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's 65 ter number 33593. It's page 16 in the English and page 15 in the B/C/S. And I'm looking for the second block of text, both languages, and the second paragraph in BOTH languages, beginning: "Some local Serbs from Srebrenica ..." And what this witness is describing is crimes that took place in 1992, and in this paragraph he says: "Some local Serbs from Srebrenica helped their Muslim neighbours during these same events," and he gives a list of the names of the survivors. And in the second bottom line, we see the name Azem Pasalic. And then in parentheses, we see: "(Died during the breakthrough from Srebrenica towards Tuzla in July 1995)."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, so far as we could tell, there was no other reference to Azem Pasalic in this statement. So given this is the example you were discussing in your examination-in-chief when you told the Bench that you had selected exclusively examples where the person giving the statement sees the person die, how do you know that this person saw Azem Pasalic die?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is not saying explicitly that he had seen this person die during the breakthrough. I don't know how. But on the other hand, it tells me that, unfortunately, I was right talking about this list and saying that some items remained from the working version, that they were not cleaned out, leaving only those who were seen to die.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's say -- did you do any follow-up on Azem Pasalic? Did you look for any other information about him?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I checked where the person was found. That was my procedure, so I know. Whether I did something in addition in this particular case I cannot tell you. If he doesn't feature in the statement of some other witness saying that he had seen this person, if I found him only in this statement and not in any other, that means that's what I managed to find and see where the person was exhumed. This falls in the categories of persons who could be interesting, but the witness does not explicitly say he had seen the death. That's why I didn't single him out for my final overview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Pavlovic, we haven't seen this final overview, but you talk about finding Azem Pasalic in a witness statement. We found him in his widow's witness statement. So I'd just like to show that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33608, and I'd like page 2 in the English and page 1 in the B/C/S to start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that. Witness, did you intend to say that that's why you did single him out for your overview or you did not single him out, which sounds a bit illogical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not include him in the final list. I know which principle I followed when working --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that clarifies the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we look in English in the first block of text seven lines from the bottom and the B/C/S, it's six lines from the bottom of the page, if you look for the date July 1993, you will see a sentence that says: "I married Azem Pasalic in July 1993 and moved to Srebrenica, where I continued to live till the beginning of July 1995 ..." And if we can turn to page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, please. Yes, now this is a fairly solid block of text, but both references are approximately halfway down. If you look for the name Dragan Trisic. And just while you're finding that, I'll tell you that the witness is talking about Potocari on 13th July 1995. And what the witness says is: "At around 1530 hours, Dragan Trisic, who was among the Chetniks, came up to my husband and was saying to him that he would help us with getting on the truck. My husband and I started towards the truck at 1600 hours, when a Chetnik grabbed my husband by the shoulder and took him off the truck, because I heard Dragan Trisic say, Take him off, damn him, he's rich, following which, they took my husband to an unfinished house, into which I saw them take seven people more, as of when I have not seen my husband ..." So, Mr. Pavlovic, the last time Azem Pasalic is seen alive by his widow he's being separated at Potocari and taken off to the unfinished house there; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And somehow you found the statement that referenced him dying in the breakthrough but you didn't manage to find the statement of his widow talking about the last time she saw him alive.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm not disputing that this is the same person, but I worked on statements made by people who participated in the breakthrough. I did not look into the statements of wives and other persons who were transported by bus from Potocari to Kladanj, so it's not strange why I've never read this statement. I was focussing on the statements of people who participated in the breakthrough and who testified about the circumstances of that breakthrough. My working list included everything that could potentially be interesting. Only in the second stage did I do some more checking to see whether anyone had seen them die.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And when you say "second stage," that's this shorter overview that you've been working on but that we haven't seen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when did you finalize this shorter -- when was it created, this new list and ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While I was here during preparation. I finalized it here, trying to exclude everything that was not 100 per cent certain. At least based on the available information. You can never have 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. When you were here. You were here in December. You are here now in January. Do you mean in December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the list you gave to the Defence a couple of days before the start of your testimony, that you were able to verify so many details and were, thus, able to create a new list within two, three days? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was almost finished when I brought it. I just looked at the statements and I saw whether the witness was saying a person had died before their eyes. That's -- that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You reviewed all those statements in the last couple of days before you came to this courtroom to further filter your earlier results?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said that job was almost finished. And it's not a big job. There are a maximum of 20, 30 such statements. I could just check that particular detail, what the witness was saying about the death of a particular person I was looking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm still puzzled by the fact that nothing of the kind was brought to our attention in December, but let's leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one other question. Sir, when you -- excuse me. When you handed this list to the Defence, did you not keep a copy for yourself to be able to testify from it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I came here it was a bit chaotic because they didn't have my material at all. Everything was blocked, all the files, all the computers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I stop you -- can I stop you? Did you not keep a copy for yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I would have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you -- I take it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did a lot of work here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that's in electronic format. It's not just typed out, handwritten. Are you telling us that you do not know whether have you even an electronic copy of the final version of your list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had it and I handed it over in electronic form. Whether I still have it, whether it remains somewhere, I have to look. I didn't look into it before, because I had no idea the situation was as it is, that the list we have here is wrong or that the wrong list was disclosed or whatever you call it. I would have to check where that list is. It exists because I know I made it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But do I understand you really well that you had an electronic version, that you gave that electronic version apparently in some -- on a stick or whatever way, to the Defence without knowing for sure that you kept an electronic copy or original of that electronic version you gave to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't get me wrong, I just don't dare to say anything that would later prove to be a mistake. I just want to be sure about what I'm saying, so I need to check. If you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you look at your final list over the last month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because that list remained with the Defence. I didn't know which version was disclosed here, so I didn't pay attention. I had no reason to look into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you gave it to the Defence, how did you give it to the Defence? Was it a written, hard copy? Was it, you said, electronic version? How did you give it to the Defence? Did you have a memory stick, or did you have -- what kind of -- how did you transfer these data to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember exactly because we worked 12 hours per day. It was chaos. We were rushing to finish it all. Now how specifically I handed it over, I don't know. I can't remember at which moment I handed it over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you really don't remember whether you used a USB stick or whether you burned it on a CD or -- or that you sent it electronically by mail as a -- you have no idea?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not provide it on a CD. It could have been done on the laptop of Mr. Lukic. Because sometimes I used his laptop to finish certain things. I told you, it was chaos, we worked 12 hours per day. I can't remember exactly. It could have been either on a memory stick or on his laptop, but I never used any CDs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But on his laptop, you said most of that work had been done before you arrived. It was only a small portion that still had to be done. You wouldn't have done that on his laptop when you were still in -- at home, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I finished it here. I just finalized it. Now whether ... whether I copied it from a memory stick to his laptop, that's the detail I can't remember. We did a lot of things during those few days. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, time to review your own laptop, I'm afraid. That's -- but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just before we do, Mr. Pavlovic, do you have any idea how many names would be on this short and final list that you say you gave to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I would have to go through it and see how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, I ask because you saw this list extensively during your examination-in-chief. I mean, you mentioned I think it was seven names from it, from different pages. You didn't notice at any point in your examination-in-chief that you were using the unfinalized list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know by heart the contents of all the statements. The volume of the material I worked with is huge. I couldn't know by heart what each statement states about a particular person. I would like to be that kind of genius but I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's not what I'm -- that's not what I'm asking you, Mr. Pavlovic. I'm asking if you noticed at any point whether you were using the wrong list. But I take it from your answer, you did not.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It never occurred to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it occurred to you now during cross-examination that this is the wrong list? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I saw that in the specific case concerning sanitizations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You were shown the page on sanitization during your examination-in-chief and you spoke about two of the names from that list, but you didn't notice then that there were four other names on it that you say shouldn't have been there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I looked at it without noticing because I wasn't focussing on that. You just asked me about a few persons who shouldn't be there. That's how I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to another example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can go back to the list, MFI D01399, page 5 in both languages. I'm looking for the name Mujo Turkovic, he is second bottom in the English, Your Honours. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now you mention two witnesses here and I don't want to read out the name of the -- of the first one, we'll come back to him. But the first witness does say according to -- or, rather, your list does say according to the witness's statement he died around Kamenica. And then you mention a second witness. And you say: "As well, according to Ademovic Sevala, seen to have died."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So let's look at the statement for Mr. Ademovic. It is 1D06277, and I'd like page 3 in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Of course. 1D06277.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, the second-last paragraph in both languages, beginning: "Finally, I would like to point out ..." And here it says: "Finally, I would like to point out that the following died in the breakthrough towards Tuzla." And the second-last name, that's Mujo Turkovic. So in your list, you represent this person as saying Mujo Turkovic was seen to have died. How -- how do you get that from this witness statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This witness is mentioned in a different place. I just said in a comment that he also mentions him, but I'm not sure if the witness first witness saw him directly, so I don't know. In principle, this is just additional information in this specific case, that there are two persons, two witnesses who mention that this particular person lost his life during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was going to say but is the statement of the one who says he has seen him die that are you being shown now -- am I not ... is this not Ademovic's statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the one who says he saw him die. So it's not the other witness. It's the same witness, Mr. Pavlovic. Now, he is not saying he saw him die in his statement. The question the Prosecution is asking how -- where did you get it from that he saw him die which you wrote in your report? Could you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My table says that this witness saw him die, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your table says, Mr. Pavlovic: "As well, according to Ademovic Sevala, seen to have died."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, did I the state in the comment that this witness also saw him die.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go back to the list so we have it on our screen in front of us, MFI D01399. It's page 5 in both languages. It's the fourth from the top in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now you can see the comment, Mr. Pavlovic. I'd invite you to answer His Honour Judge Moloto's question.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads here: "As well, according to Ademovic Sevala, seen to have died." It doesn't say that Ademovic Sevala saw him die but that he was seen to have died, because Sevala said they also died during the breakthrough. Whether he himself saw him, we cannot say 100 per cent that he didn't. Perhaps he did or he heard from somebody who was close to him, but someone saw him die. There must be a way to take over statements about the circumstances of this, whether Sevala Ademovic saw him die or whether somebody else saw him die and then told him. I don't see anything disputable about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, what's the source of your claim that someone saw Mujo Turkovic die?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the first person, the first witness, whose name we mustn't mention. But let me say again, because I see there are other instances where it was not just seen, I cannot claim that the first witness saw him for sure because I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, that's the reason why I'm asking you: What is the basis for your claim that someone saw Mujo Turkovic die?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look, I refer to witness statements where they say that the person died during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the Prosecution is the one that has to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. -- you are claiming in this courtroom whether Sevala Ademovic saw him die or somebody else saw him die and told him: "I don't see anything disputable about this." Do you have a source saying that that source saw Mr. Turkovic die, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot claim with 100 per cent certainty because I don't know what the first witness stated. Perhaps he did say so, but I don't know it off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I leave it in the hands of -- but the interesting matter is that it's in relation to this second witness that you say "seen." So there there's a visual observation. And that's, I think, also in your own language. If I'm not mistake the word "vizin" [phoen] refers to a visual observation. You put it for the second witness. Now you say it could be the first one. So let's then check -- I take it, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could we move into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now like to turn to the statement of the first witness, and for that, I'm sorry I didn't just mention this, I'd like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then that's what can happen. We return -- we now move again into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, you were going to find out from the witness whether this is the statement he used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, do you remember if the statement that I've just read to you that we just looked at in private session, if that is the statement you used for your conclusion about what this witness said about Mujo Turkovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this statement. I used it during my work, but I did not draw the conclusion that this person was killed during the breakthrough when I put that in my final table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We'll come to that in a moment. But according to this witness statement we've just read - and, for the record, also according to the one in evidence, Your Honours - this witness last saw Mujo Turkovic alive in the custody of the VRS on a meadow, being taken to a nearby house. That's what we've just seen, isn't it? I need you to answer verbally, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if we can go back to your list again, D01399 MFI. Page 5 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S, and I'm just going to read out what it says in the description: "According to," the witness's statement, "he died around Kamenica." Now, what you said in your list, that's not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in the first part of the statement, the last one that we saw, the witness says that the person was wounded in that area and remained there, and only in the second part of the statement, if I remember this well, that he returned or picked him up and brought him, we saw where and how. This is just a statement from the working stage of my analysis. When reading the witness statements, I included all persons who could be interesting, and obviously this remained from the working -- or older version of my analysis where I included all persons who could be suspicious and then -- because I attached the statement of the protected witness and I'm familiar with it, so why would I bring it here and why would I do that? It would be quite illogical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Witness, in your report, if you have read that statement of the witness, first of all, you do not say interesting witnesses -- witness. You clearly say, according to that witness, he died; whereas in the statement, whether in the full version as you told us a second ago or only in the portion read to you, it doesn't say at all that he died there. It says that he was wounded and taken over by the soldiers. So even if it's a working document, why would you include in that working document information which is flatly not in line with what that statement says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the working stage while reading witness statements of those who have participated in the breakthrough, I included people who were seen to have died, seen by the witnesses, and persons about whom they heard they had died, and also those who were wounded and left somewhere, so that I could go back. Because many of the wounded remained at the locations where they were left and then died there, so I wanted to see where a person was found. Because a person may have been seen as being wounded at Kamenica, above Kravica, and then later sanitized from that location. So that's why I included -- I simply included or inserted the information during the working stage of the process so that I could then go through it all once again and check. That was why such persons can be found there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like to move to another example, Mr. Pavlovic. If we can go to page 3 in both languages of your list and the name I'm looking for is Ragib Mehmedovic. He is three from the bottom in the English and five from the top in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to the witness before you put your question, Mr. MacDonald. This name, does it appear in your final list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name we just commented on or the one that we are about to comment on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The one we are about to comment on, Ragib Mehmedovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't know that off the top of my head which persons are included in the lists. Really, it's impossible for me to know that. I would have to memorize many names and statements. Simply, there's no need for me to remember them when I relied on having everything on paper. Because, let me repeat again, I've gone through a lot of data --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, nothing to -- no reason to repeat anything. You don't know. Thank you. Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, the reason I'd like to bring this victim to your attention is that you actually used the same witness statement, the witness statement of Sevala Ademovic, to say that this person also died during the breakthrough. Do you see that on the screen in front of you? Now --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says according to Ademovic Sevala's statement, died through breakthrough, found in such-and-such mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now I wonder if we could go back into private session, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session -- we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, you read this statement, and we won't refer to the name of the -- of the person who gave it, and according to that statement, the last time Ragib Mehmedovic is seen alive, he is sitting on that meadow under guard. Why did you not mention this in your list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it exactly the same person?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Is the witness or the victim?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, in the witness statement, you'll recall it says Ragib Mehmedovic, son of Rasim. And that's what you've got written in your list, and I would say that you, of course, refer to Sevala Ademovic's statement who you used for the other victim, Mujo Turkovic. So, yes, I'm fairly certain it's the same person, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's the same person, we have statements of two witnesses who testify about two different circumstances about one and the same person, that is to say, victim. The only way to establish who of the two of them is right is to take statements from these witnesses about additional circumstances, where they saw him, who saw him, where, under what circumstances. And for me to say how he really lost his life, that's something I'm unable to do, whether he was really taken prisoner or died during the breakthrough. We have two different statements of two different witnesses. If it's one and the same person. Because there are many persons who have the same first and last names, even father's names and sometimes the place of residence. But I do not exclude the possibility that this may be the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You'll remember that Sevala Ademovic doesn't say that he saw him die. He just says the following died during the breakthrough, whereas the other witness is much more precise. Mr. Pavlovic, what I asked you was: Why did you not mention that this other witness talks about Ragib Mehmedovic, son of Rasim? Why did you not mention it on your list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes. The witness who claims that the person died during breakthrough does not say that he didn't see him. We don't know whether he saw him or not. And another thing, why didn't I. I've already told you that in terms of statements I only focussed on the losses during the breakthrough whenever that was mentioned. So I probably went through all of this quite fast and I probably oversaw this, I missed it. There's nothing else for me to say, because it's obvious here that these are persons who were taken prisoner. But that was not the subject of my report, so I didn't focus on that and probably that was why I missed the fact that the person is mentioned here and in the other statement as well. So I don't dispute that I may have made a mistake. Of course, that that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, this list, both parts of it, they involved clearly a lot of work, and you have expressed to the Chamber that you were doing a great deal of work. Did you have any help, perhaps like research assistants or things, some people like that, that helped you put together this list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the part that involved analysis and search for documents, no. Because I was told I was the only person supposed to have access to them, and I focussed on what I was told. The circumstances in which the column was breaking out, an estimate of the number who got killed during the breakthrough, and possibly where the bodies could have ended up. So nobody could have access, apart from me, in this part of the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Time for the break, it is. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, you want already a new item on the screens?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I was hoping we could have Mr. Pavlovic's list, D01399 MFI, for Mr. Pavlovic coming in. As always, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is not the objection, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I searched my hard disk, external hard disk on which I have Mr. Pavlovic's documents. I found larger version. This one that was uploaded has six pages in B/C/S and seven pages in English of this document. Then we have another document, you know, then we have Excel spreadsheet attached, but this type of document, B/C/S, six; English, seven pages. What I have here is 14 pages in B/C/S. Obviously some redactions were made but I cannot locate redaction with -- on this one we can find those four names Mr. Pavlovic mentioned that should be redacted as well. So at this moment I have just the larger version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both versions you have, there is still the four numbers with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- two of them with primary graves are -- in both versions they are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those four names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In versions I located by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pavlovic, just assuming that you still have an electronic copy somewhere, could you copy that and make that electronically available to the Chamber. The easiest way is to just send it as an attachment to an e-mail address that will then be given to you. Is that a possibility? Do you have possibility to have e-mail exchanges from your hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and I'll do that with pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would you do that the first thing after you leave this courtroom to immediately send the newest version so that it be received by the -- by the Registry. I invite the -- Madam Registrar to provide an e-mail address which -- at which the witness could send it so that the parties have an opportunity to further study it and not to have to wait until late afternoon. So would you please do that, if we finish at quarter past 2.00, if possible by 3.00, or just have a sandwich for lunch and the first thing to do is to provide us with the newest version of your list, the one referred to several times today. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As soon as I find it I'll send it. I'll start looking as soon as I get back to the hotel. It is really in my interests to hand it over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, Madam Registrar, I take it that you'll select an e-mail address in which you'll find it and then it to be distributed to the parties and to the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we can help ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to tell you the longer version I have was created, at least on my computer, on the 11th of December. And this version that was uploaded was created on the 13th of December last year. So maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the witness could have --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- Mr. Pavlovic can use it in his search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we understand that the list that is being used in court so far was created after the other one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's on the 13th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the one of the 11th is not a clean-up of the one of the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a bigger document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a bigger document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pavlovic, is there any chance that the version we are looking at at this moment is already the shorter version you talked about? Because on the basis of what Mr. Lukic tells us, he apparently received two versions, both almost immediately before you arrived here in the courtroom. The 13th of December being one day before you started your testimony because I think that was on the 14th of December that you appeared in court. Is there any chance that the version we're looking at at this moment is already the shorter version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could be shorter, but it's obviously wrong. It's not the one I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we're looking forward to receiving early this afternoon a newer version without those mistakes. And could you tell us in what format that is, is it Word format or is it -- part of it was apparently in Excel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was Word and Excel, and then it was converted into PDF and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- merged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And merged --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Merged as PDF.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please send it to us in the original format, that is, Word and Excel, rather than to PDF it, to scan it and have it made a PDF format, but rather the original formats. Even if that would be two documents. But that's what we would prefer to receive. Mr. MacDonald will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: One request from the Prosecution, Your Honours. Mr. Lukic said that the second list was created on 13th December. I wonder if he has the time stamp on that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably, I have European -- I think I have 24 hour on this computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then it's the morning hours. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, one question on this -- on the creation of this list before we go back into the examples. You spoke in cross-examination for the first time about how there had been this shortened version of the list but at no point did you mention that you'd made two shortened versions, that you had shortened it once and then shortened it again. You didn't mention that in cross-examination, did you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that I worked on it and that I was finalizing it after coming here. I don't know where the last version ended up. The one we are looking at is not that one. Because I have worked on it, and I know how I proceed. It's ridiculous that I've -- that I would have released something like this as a final version. It would be less than serious to say the least.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at one more example from this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 in both languages, MFI D01399. I'm looking for the name Salko Hrnjic, son of Mehmed, 1961, second from the top in B/C/S; fourth from the top in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, in your description part, you say he died with Muhamed Mehmedovic in Snagovo, and you cite to the witness statement of Cikaric Zijad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Before we go into this example in any detail, can we turn to page 4 in both languages B/C/S. Perhaps page 5 in the English, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, at the top in the English and midway down in the B/C/S, we see a Salko Hrnjic, son of Mehmed, 1961. According to the statement of Cikaric Zijad, he died on Snagovo with Muhamed Mehmedovic. So this is a duplication in your list, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is one more proof that this is a working version of the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, in the list we have in front of us, in the list that has been uploaded, this is a duplication, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we go one page back in the English and it's at the bottom, and it's just one row up on the same page in the B/C/S, we see the name Muhamed Mehmedovic. And in the description according to Cikaric Zijad's statement, he died on Snagovo. So this is another duplication; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I can mention the name of this victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 6 from the top ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Is the name you're looking for Muhamed Mehmedovic? Because if it is, then you can mention his name.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. If you say it's a duplication, I don't know if that man is mentioned anywhere else in that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 2 in both languages of the list, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And the name Salko Hrnjic, you have in the description that a Muhamed Mehmedovic died with him in Snagovo. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. And it's in the comments where we just link them up as having died together, but it is not in the column where the list of victims is given. It's just a comment that the two persons died together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, in the interests of time, I'm not going to into in Cikaric Zijad's statement but it's been uploaded by the Defence and they're welcome to check what I'm about to say. But that person says that he sees four decomposing bodies at Snagovo, that he knew two of them, and he names Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic. Did you come across anybody else who referenced Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember off the cuff whether anyone else had seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If you can't remember, that's fine. You can just say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder if we can turn into private session, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, you'd agree with me that, according to the testimony of this witness, Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic were executed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that Salko Hrnjic got separated from the group earlier, that he was not together with the group of captives? Maybe I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm afraid you did misunderstand, Mr. Pavlovic. It was Husein Hrnjic who was separated earlier from the group. I'm afraid Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic were still with the group when the witness was taken away from it and then when he heard gun-fire. Do you agree with me, Mr. Pavlovic, that according to the testimony of this witness, Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic were the victims of summary execution?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The Defence were in possession of that testimony, Mr. Pavlovic, and clearly you found the name Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic in the witness statement of Cikaric Zijad. How did you miss this testimony about these two people?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that I dealt with statements that concerned the breakthrough and losses during the breakthrough. That's what I focussed on. Why did I miss it? It's logical that I missed it. I didn't consider captured persons. This is a transcript of witness evidence, whereas I studied the circumstances of what happened during the breakthrough and persons who were seen to have been killed during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, this is an incident of summary execution of people in the column. Are you telling the Court that when you read these statements, as soon as people are captured, even names that you're interested in, you simply stop reading and ignore what happens to them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a transcript. When I searched the database, I was looking for statements and I focussed on statements in order to get some information. Whether that information was completely correct or not, whether it was complete or not, I think this process is designed precisely to find that out. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And, Mr. Pavlovic, I take it --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, when I say "statements" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Pavlovic, that you would say, now that I brought these two examples to your attention, that these two also didn't make this final shortened list that we haven't seen as of yet.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If witnesses in the statements they gave to security agencies or to your investigators, if they say in these statements that they had seen someone die, I would include these persons in the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Given -- I see the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give us a clue as to where we are in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm finished with the list, Your Honours. I would propose to deal tomorrow morning with two examples that Mr. Pavlovic cites in his report and thereafter finish. And I hope --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be less than half an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I hope so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's what we'll then try to do tomorrow. Before we adjourn, Mr. Pavlovic, I am seeking clarification on one issue. Mr. MacDonald asked you something about the second shorter version, because Mr. Lukic told us there was a longer version, then there was the version we have at this moment which was the shorter one, and you explained to us that, since then, there was another even shorter version. And let me just read what you said because that's what I would like to have further clarified. Mr. MacDonald asked you why it is now for the first time that you're -- and whether you had shortened the document, the list, once and then shortened it again. You didn't mention that in cross-examination. That was the question that was put to you. And your answer was the following. You said: "I have said that I worked on it and that I was finalizing it after coming here." And then you say: "I don't know where the last version ended up." Now what I'm seeking clarification of is the following line. You said: "... and that I was finalizing it after coming here." Did you mean to say that you worked on finalizing it after you had arrived in The Hague but still in The Hague, or that you worked on it and yet you were finalizing it after coming here? That means after you -- after your testimony, after your stay here in The Hague? Could you tell us what you meant when you said "I was finalizing it after coming here"? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked on the document in the phase of preparation before beginning to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So "after coming here" means after your arrival but before giving your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not anymore when you had left The Hague after you had given your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I felt no need. I didn't even know that there was a mixup.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. So the version -- well, let's say, when you left The Hague, you had prepared the final version, and you didn't work on it any further since then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was practically finished that last day, the last evening. Because we were doing several things at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Practically finished" means what? Was it finished or was it not finished? Did you work on it any further after that evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. Before. Before testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, only maybe Mr. Pavlovic should be provided with the document that is in the e-court, so we have printed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why does he --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing he should do is to give us the latest version and there's no need for him to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but to check maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To check or not -- I mean, I think the checking will be done by any interested parties --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he knows that it's not the version he -- you need. That was just my proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, what we expect the witness to do is, we have one before us which was tendered --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the witness says there's another one. He doesn't have to compare. Let him give us the latest version he has in his possession. And, Mr. Pavlovic, we're very much looking forward to receiving that by -- well, if not by 3.00, then perhaps by 3.30. Let's adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning where there will be another approximately half an hour of cross-examination and then you will be reexamined by Mr. Lukic. I instruct you again, as I did before, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, either already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning. You may now follow the usher. And you will be provided with the e-mail address to which you can send the original, although final versions of -- most likely -- well, in whatever format not scanned and PDF'd after that. Madam Registrar, you have provided the witness with that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will as soon as we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn for the day -- you may already follow the usher and then we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, the 2nd of February, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of February, 2016, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
